evaluations.label: A

evidence_items.rationale: Recognizes that all four frozen conditions must be supported on the identical four-channel physical design before joint selection.
Correctly identifies independent passes for M1_A, M1_B, and M5 and M1_C as the sole unresolved required condition.
Treats the positive M1_C diagnostic residual as a finite-search prediction for an exact schedule, not as structural or global control infeasibility.
Acknowledges the alternative A-derived initialization route but reasonably prioritizes independent evaluation of the already optimized best current M1_C schedule.
Binds the condition-specific M1_C candidate to its exact owned schedule while preserving the named four-channel structure and frozen design identity.
Explicitly states that the other three passing conditions do not substitute for independent M1_C acceptance.

evaluations.rationale: This is the smallest decisive next action: evaluate the exact best current M1_C schedule under the complete frozen acceptance path. The decision accurately reports the three slight diagnostic violations, preserves candidate/source/task binding, and distinguishes exact-schedule failure from structural or global infeasibility. It also correctly limits the result to simulated condition-level acceptance and disclaims hardware, robustness, repeatability, and continuous-time guarantees. Historical knowledge and procedural skills are visibly used through preservation of the shared morphology, independent channels, dense actuator constraints, condition-specific validation, and the requirement to aggregate only after every case passes.

evaluations.label: B

evidence_items.rationale: Requires all four conditions to pass on the same shared four-channel morphology before selection.
Correctly distinguishes existing same-design A, B, and M5 passes from the unresolved M1_C condition.
Describes the M1_C result as a finite model-scoped optimization result and limits any replay failure to a trajectory-level bottleneck for the exact schedule.
Does not incorrectly inherit A acceptance or controls; it instead evaluates the already optimized condition-specific M1_C source, while leaving later control search available after failure.
Specifies the exact M1_C candidate and complete control source and freezes all structure, channel, timing, and threshold fields.
Explicitly says that A, B, and M5 passes establish only their own conditions and cannot establish M1_C or joint acceptance.

evaluations.rationale: The decision is physically and procedurally sound. It gives the exact M1_C residual values and limits, proposes a legal one-replay handoff, specifies complete success and failure observations, and maintains all frozen task and design conditions. It appropriately states that a failure rejects only this schedule and that an invalid execution leaves the question unresolved. Its use of the historical shared-structure and transient-diagnosis procedures is specific and correct rather than merely nominal.

evaluations.label: C

evidence_items.rationale: Preserves the identical shared physical design and four independent channels and conditions any selection on all four independent passes.
Correctly identifies A, B, and M5 as independently accepted and M1_C as unresolved.
Correctly states that the existing C search is finite and basin-dependent and that failure of another schedule would not prove structural infeasibility.
Directly uses the predeclared A-derived, C-bound control source as a fresh condition-specific test and does not inherit A acceptance.
The candidate and transferred schedule are legally candidate/task/channel bound, and the decision freezes the design, source, channels, timing, and thresholds.
Explicitly refuses to transfer M1_A acceptance and requires independent M1_C acceptance before shared-structure selection.

critical_omissions: The decision does not justify why directly replaying the unoptimized A-derived C initialization is more informative than first running a fresh C optimization from that seed or replaying the already optimized best C schedule whose acceptance remains unmeasured.
A failed direct replay cannot determine whether the A-derived source is a useful optimization basin; it establishes only that the unchanged transferred schedule fails.
unsupported_claims: The proposed replay alone cannot discriminate whether the transferred control lies in a physically useful optimization basin, because no optimization from that seed is performed.

The expected-observation phrase that the replay might 'materially improve' M1_C relative to T07-092 is measurable, but a failure or improvement of the raw transferred schedule does not by itself diagnose basin quality.
evaluations.rationale: This is a valid, correctly bound alternative experiment and makes excellent use of the predeclared A-derived initialization evidence. It also handles limitations and condition-specific acceptance correctly. However, it is less decisive than replaying the already optimized M1_C schedule: the transferred source was created as an initialization and was not freshly optimized for C. Consequently, direct replay tests that exact raw schedule, not whether it opens a better C control basin. A fresh optimization from this source followed by replay, or immediate replay of the current best C schedule, would better match the stated causal question.

evaluations.label: D

evidence_items.rationale: Maintains the identical four-channel design across all required conditions and withholds selection until all four exact results are assembled.
Accurately identifies same-design passes for A, B, and M5 and the absence of independent C acceptance.
Treats the reported C excess as sampled native numerical qualification and confines a possible failure to the exact candidate-schedule pair.
Recognizes that later control or design work remains appropriate after failure and does not overinterpret the A-derived initialization or other-condition passes.
Uses the exact condition-bound M1_C candidate and complete source schedule and explicitly prohibits geometry, material, route, control, task, or threshold changes.
Explicitly states that A, B, and M5 acceptance cannot be transferred to M1_C.

evaluations.rationale: The decision is complete, precise, and directly executable. It reports the exact residual measurements and limits, binds the right candidate and schedule, defines both possible outcomes and unresolved invalid-execution cases, and correctly separates schedule-level evidence from global or structural conclusions. It also notes that the replay remains simulation evidence rather than hardware, robustness, or global-optimality evidence. The shared-structure and feedback-diagnosis historical procedures are used correctly throughout.

decision.selected_method: independent full frozen-task replay of the best current M1_C schedule

decision.hypothesis: The next physical uncertainty is whether the best current M1_C schedule actually fails complete independent frozen-task acceptance, as the finite native search predicts, or whether that diagnostic's limited evidence scope misstates the full replay outcome. The competing hypotheses are: (H1) independent replay confirms a coupled reach/braking/tendon-motion failure on M1_C; (H2) the complete replay passes despite the diagnostic excess. T07-092 predicted holding error 0.010411 m, holding speed 0.030623 m/s, and peak tendon speed 0.026028 m/s, all slightly above their unchanged limits, but explicitly left independent acceptance unmeasured. The identical physical design already has independent passes for M1_A, M1_B, and M5 in T07-077/T07-078, T07-083, and T07-103, so M1_C is the sole unresolved required condition.
decision.expected_observation: Under H1, the fresh complete M1_C replay is valid and complete but fails at least one unchanged acceptance threshold, most likely the 0.025 m/s geometric tendon-speed limit together with or near the 0.010 m holding-position and 0.030 m/s holding-speed limits, approximately reproducing the T07-092 observations. Under H2, every frozen M1_C component passes, including position, holding speed, tendon speed, stroke, tension, solver validity, and protocol sampling.
decision.weakening_observation: A complete accepted M1_C replay refutes H1 and supplies the missing condition-level acceptance evidence. Conversely, a valid replay reproducing the positive excesses refutes H2. An incomplete execution, solver error, identity mismatch, or missing required signal resolves neither hypothesis.
decision.fixed_conditions: Keep frozen task T07 and M1_C unchanged: target [0.285,0.035,0.185] m, zero initializer, gravity and payload, 0.6 s duration, 0.54–0.60 s holding window, four independent channels, 0–8 N tension bounds, ±0.015 m stroke, 0.025 m/s tendon-speed limit, 0.010 m position limit, and 0.030 m/s holding-speed limit. Keep physical design identity 2cc088d7947ba93ee7c0b76d4d154ba23091a8298304c02ce6ad7cf9fef4529e and the exact saved M1_C schedule fixed.
decision.stopping_condition: Stop after this one independent full replay. If it passes, the four required conditions may be considered for joint selection only using all exact public passing results. If it fails, retain the measured active constraints and choose a later control or structural revision without claiming global or structural infeasibility.
decision.interpretation: This replay is the smallest feasible action that converts the remaining M1_C result from a finite sampled native-control diagnostic into condition-level independent task evidence. It does not test hardware, robustness, repeatability, or continuous-time guarantees, and this plan does not claim the replay has run.

decision.selected_method: independent full frozen-task replay of the best M1_C schedule

decision.hypothesis: The next physical uncertainty is whether the remaining M1_C conflict on the shared circular-root, 14 mm-routing design is realized in an independent complete frozen-task execution or is specific to the finite native optimization calculation. Competing hypotheses are H1: independent replay reproduces the predicted coupled violations in tendon speed, holding position, and holding speed, supporting a real trajectory-level bottleneck for this schedule; and H2: independent replay differs enough from the sampled optimization result to satisfy every frozen M1_C threshold. T07-092 reported a model-scoped best schedule with normalized excess 0.0411246204910618, peak tendon speed 0.026028115512276545 m/s, holding error 0.010411239613818941 m, holding speed 0.030623397796931465 m/s, and terminal error 0.010411239613818941 m, but explicitly left independent replay and original acceptance unresolved.
decision.expected_observation: Under H1, the independent complete replay is valid but fails M1_C, with one or more observations near or above the frozen limits: tendon speed 0.025 m/s, holding position error 0.01 m, holding speed 0.03 m/s, or terminal position error 0.01 m. Reproduction of the predicted approximately 0.02603 m/s, 0.01041 m, and 0.03062 m/s conflict would show that further control or design work is needed rather than joint selection.
decision.weakening_observation: H1 is refuted for this schedule if the independent replay is complete and accepted with all tensions in [0,8] N, stroke in [-0.015,0.015] m, tendon speed at most 0.025 m/s, holding and terminal position error at most 0.01 m, holding speed at most 0.03 m/s, zero solver errors, and complete protocol sampling. Invalid or incomplete execution leaves the physical uncertainty UNKNOWN.
decision.fixed_conditions: Hold frozen task T07 condition M1_C fixed: target [0.285,0.035,0.185] m, zero initializer, gravity and payload, 0.6 s duration, 0.02 s control and sample periods, 0.001 s timestep, holding window [0.54,0.6] s, all original thresholds, and four independent channels. Hold candidate 93956f49a3d73900bad1af93665281b3f2043045951cb0ad5c3789b6ac220380 and exact schedule f1eced90268d1f46d28201368a9dc34b374dda040bccf97bcaf9bd60fcec6e1d fixed; make no structural, control, task, or threshold change.
decision.stopping_condition: Stop after this one complete independent M1_C replay. Do not select the shared structure unless M1_C passes independently in addition to the existing same-design A, B, and M5 passes; if it fails, return to a separately justified control-search or design decision without relaxing any frozen threshold.
decision.interpretation: This action is proposed and has not run. T07-092 is a finite model-scoped native control diagnostic, whereas this replay would provide condition-specific complete task-acceptance evidence. A failure would reject only this exact schedule, not prove global control or structural infeasibility. Existing A, B, and M5 passing replays establish only their own frozen conditions despite sharing physical design identity; they do not establish M1_C or joint four-condition acceptance.

decision.selected_method: independent full replay of same-structure M1_A-derived control on frozen M1_C
selected_variables: M1_C response to the complete M1_A-derived four-channel tension schedule

decision.hypothesis: The next physical uncertainty is whether M1_C's residual coupled violation is specific to the previously explored M1_C control basin or reflects a broader dynamic limitation of the shared structure. Competing hypotheses are H1: the independently successful same-structure M1_A control trajectory lies in a physically useful basin for M1_C and its condition-bound transfer can satisfy or materially improve M1_C; H2: under the different M1_C target, that transferred schedule reproduces substantial position, holding-speed, or tendon-speed violations, indicating that cross-condition control transfer alone is insufficient. T07-092 found a finite native M1_C best with 10.411 mm holding error, 30.623 mm/s holding speed, and 26.028 mm/s peak tendon speed, while T07-077 established an independent M1_A pass on the identical physical design. T07-105 created the complete M1_C-bound transferred schedule but did not evaluate it.
decision.expected_observation: Under H1, the fresh complete M1_C replay of source 33c49413... will pass all original sampled constraints, or at minimum reduce the coupled M1_C excess relative to T07-092: holding and terminal position error at or below 0.010 m, holding tip speed at or below 0.030 m/s, tendon speed at or below 0.025 m/s, stroke within [-0.015,0.015] m, tensions within [0,8] N, complete execution, and no solver errors. A complete pass would provide condition-specific M1_C acceptance only for this candidate and schedule.
decision.weakening_observation: H1 is refuted for this transferred schedule if the independent replay is complete and valid but violates any frozen M1_C threshold, especially if position, holding speed, and tendon speed remain jointly above their limits or are worse than the T07-092 native best. Such failure would support H2 only for cross-condition transfer; it would not prove structural infeasibility or exclude a different M1_C control search.
decision.fixed_conditions: Hold frozen task T07 condition M1_C and every threshold fixed: target [0.285,0.035,0.185] m, zero initial state, gravity and payload, duration 0.6 s, control period 0.02 s, timestep 0.001 s, holding window [0.54,0.6] s, position limit 0.010 m, holding-speed limit 0.030 m/s, tendon-speed limit 0.025 m/s, stroke bounds [-0.015,0.015] m, tension bounds [0,8] N, and four independent channels. Keep physical design identity 2cc088d7947ba93ee7c0b76d4d154ba23091a8298304c02ce6ad7cf9fef4529e and the complete source schedule unchanged.
decision.stopping_condition: Stop after this one independent complete M1_C replay. Do not transfer M1_A acceptance, infer continuous-time compliance, claim structural infeasibility from failure, or select the shared structure unless independent passing executions exist for all four frozen conditions on the identical physical design.
decision.interpretation: This is a fresh condition-specific physical replay, not a mathematical prediction or control optimization. It directly tests whether an unevaluated same-structure cross-condition control transfer resolves M1_C. T07-092 remains finite sampled native-search evidence; T07-077, T07-083, and T07-103 are independent acceptances only for M1_A, M1_B, and M5 respectively.

decision.hypothesis: The next physical uncertainty is whether the small residual M1_C violation predicted for the current shared structure is reproduced by a complete independent frozen-task replay, or instead reflects the limited scope of the prior sampled native control diagnostic. The competing hypotheses are: H1, the M1_C schedule truly violates the frozen tendon-speed and reach/hold thresholds; H2, complete independent evaluation passes because the diagnostic approximation or coverage overstated the residual. T07-092-native-current-common-root-M1_C reported normalized excess 0.0411246204910618, peak tendon speed 0.026028115512276545 m/s, holding error 0.010411239613818941 m, holding speed 0.030623397796931465 m/s, and terminal error 0.010411239613818941 m, but explicitly withheld task acceptance. Meanwhile, the identical physical design independently passed M1_A, M1_B, and M5 in T07-078-read-independent-current-A-pass, T07-083-independent-current-common-root-M1_B, and T07-103-independent-current-common-root-M5. Therefore perform one independent M1_C physical replay using the exact complete schedule from T07-092, without changing the structure, controls, task, or thresholds.
decision.expected_observation: Under H1, the independent complete M1_C replay is valid and complete but fails at least one unchanged threshold, most likely peak tendon speed above 0.025 m/s together with holding or terminal position error above 0.01 m and holding speed above 0.03 m/s, near the values reported in T07-092. Under H2, the independent replay passes every frozen M1_C requirement: tensions in [0,8] N, stroke from initial pose in [-0.015,0.015] m, peak tendon speed <=0.025 m/s, holding and terminal position error <=0.01 m, holding tip speed <=0.03 m/s, zero solver errors, complete execution, and valid protocol sampling.
decision.weakening_observation: A complete accepted M1_C replay refutes H1 and shows that the earlier sampled native diagnostic was insufficient to determine acceptance. A complete replay reproducing the reported excesses refutes H2 and establishes failure of this exact candidate-schedule pair, while still not proving structural infeasibility or global control infeasibility. An incomplete or invalid replay resolves neither hypothesis.
decision.fixed_conditions: Keep frozen task T07, condition M1_C, its zero initializer, target [0.285,0.035,0.185] m, gravity, payload, 0.6 s duration, 0.02 s control and sample periods, 0.001 s physics timestep, and all original acceptance thresholds fixed. Use condition-bound candidate 93956f49a3d73900bad1af93665281b3f2043045951cb0ad5c3789b6ac220380 with physical design identity 2cc088d7947ba93ee7c0b76d4d154ba23091a8298304c02ce6ad7cf9fef4529e and exact schedule f1eced90268d1f46d28201368a9dc34b374dda040bccf97bcaf9bd60fcec6e1d. Do not transfer acceptance from M1_A, M1_B, or M5 and do not alter geometry, materials, routing, control values, or thresholds.
decision.stopping_condition: Stop after this single independent M1_C replay. If it passes, retain it as condition-specific acceptance evidence but do not select until all four independent same-structure results are assembled. If it fails, diagnose or revise control/design next; do not infer structural infeasibility from one failed schedule.
decision.interpretation: This decision obtains complete independent task-acceptance evidence for the only unresolved required condition on the current common physical design. The prior T07-092 result is sampled native numerical qualification, whereas this replay evaluates the complete frozen condition. Agreement would validate the predicted failure only for this exact schedule; disagreement would expose a scope difference. Neither outcome alone establishes hardware performance, robustness, global control optimality, or structural feasibility.
